“In our first pivotal trial readout as a company, APOLLO delivered strong and compelling evidence of the potential clinical benefit of bitopertin for patients with EPP,” said John Quisel, J.D., Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of Disc.

“Alongside our anticipated end-of-Phase 2 FDA meeting for selcodebart in anemia of myelofibrosis in the fourth quarter and a strengthened balance sheet, we are well positioned to support the anticipated launch of bitopertin and advance two additional programs toward pivotal-stage development in 2027.” Recent Highlights and Anticipated Milestones: Bitopertin: GlyT1 Inhibitor (Heme Synthesis Modulator) • Positive topline data from the Phase 3 APOLLO clinical trial of bitopertin in EPP achieved statistical significance on both co-primary endpoints of reduction in whole blood metal-free PPIX from baseline and average monthly total time in sunlight without pain during month 6 of treatment vs. placebo.
